gaps.what: relieving arches of alternating white stone and brick voussoirs over the first-storey windows, and white blocks banded through the brick piers beside every window
two step gables side by side with white-capped steps, white blocks and arched relieving bands over the gable windows
a tall white timber ground frontage across the whole wall: a row of small-paned entresol lights over doors (one round-arched) and boarded or glazed panels
a small window with its own white cornice cap sits in the valley between the two gables

notes: One wall carries two identical step gables (a double house); the left half is described. The single full upper storey runs across both halves; everything above the white band at the gable foot is in the gables.
